symptoms.symptom: My new oven doesn't cook like my old one. Is something wrong with the temperature settings?

causes.label: Your new oven has a different cooking system from your old oven and therefore may cook differently than your old oven.
remedies: For the first few uses, follow your recipe times and temperatures carefully and use rack positions recommended in the Cooking Guide.
If you still think your new oven is too hot or too cold, you can adjust the temperature yourself to meet your specific cooking preference.
See the Special Features section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 34: "Your new oven has a different cooking system from your old oven and therefore may cook differently than your old oven."

symptoms.symptom: Why is my range making a "clicking" noise when using my oven?

causes.label: Your range has been designed to maintain a tighter control over your oven's temperature.
remedies: This is normal.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 34: "Your range has been designed to maintain a tighter control over your oven's temperature."

causes.label: You may hear your oven's heating elements "click" on and off more frequently than in older ovens to achieve better results during baking, broiling, and self-clean cycles.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 34: "You may hear your oven's heating elements "click" on and off more frequently than in older ovens to achieve better results during baking, broiling, and self-clean cycles."

symptoms.symptom: Sometimes the oven takes longer to preheat to the same temperature

causes.label: Cookware, food, and/or number of racks in oven.
remedies: Cookware, food, and racks in the oven will cause differences in preheat times.
Remove excess items to reduce preheat time. 49-85221

symptoms.symptom: Top burners do not burn evenly

causes.label: Improper burner assembly.
remedies: Make sure the burner caps are seated correctly.
See the Care and Cleaning of the range section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 36: "Improper burner assembly."

causes.label: Burner slots on the side of the burner may be clogged.
remedies: Remove the burners for cleaning.
See the Care and Cleaning of the range section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 36: "Burner slots on the side of the burner may be clogged."

symptoms.symptom: Burner flames are very large or yellow

causes.label: Improper air to gas ratio.
remedies: If range is connected to Propane gas, contact the technician who installed your range or made the conversion.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 36: "Improper air to gas ratio."

symptoms.symptom: My oven door glass appears to be "tinted" or have a "rainbow" color.

causes.label: The inner oven glass is coated with a heat barrier to reflect the heat back into the oven to prevent heat loss and keep the outer door cool while baking.
remedies: This is normal.
Under certain light or angles, you may see this tint or rainbow color.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 36: "The inner oven glass is coated with a heat barrier to reflect the heat back into the oven to prevent heat loss and keep the outer door cool while baking."

symptoms.symptom: Drawer does not slide smoothly or drags

causes.label: The drawer is out of alignment.
remedies: Fully extend the drawer and push it all the way in.
See the Care and Cleaning of the range section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 36: "The drawer is out of alignment."

causes.label: Drawer is over-loaded or load is unbalanced.
remedies: Reduce weight or redistribute drawer contents. 49-85221
